text:
ana: Hey infra — prepping cross-cloud org for a new customer (Acme). Can we run a quick preflight QA for provisioning accounts/projects across AWS/GCP/Azure? Main asks: GPU quota increases, VPC/IP limits, IAM/service account patterns, billing+tags, region constraints and any gotchas. Timeline: ~3 weeks. What do I need to collect to kick off quota requests?

ryan: +1. Short checklist off the top of my head: billing account + billing owner, org/folder/project naming, target regions, desired GPU SKUs & counts, expected QPS, tags/cost-center, KMS/PEM ownership, and timeline. Also decide whether we use shared VPCs or per-project.

maria: GCP specifics: GPU quotas are per region and per GPU type (e.g., nvidia-tesla-a100). You need to open a support case for quota increases — include project number and region. Quick checks: 
```
# check quotas
gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --project=PROJECT_ID
# check GPU quota usage
gcloud compute accelerators describe --region=us-west1
```
Also watch out for accelerators being available only in certain zones. Shared VPC: create host project, attach service projects, give service accounts 'compute.serviceAgent' roles.

samir: AWS notes: Use Service Quotas console or CLI to request EC2 GPU instance quotas (p4d, p3). Also check ENI and Private IPv4 address quotas — those bite us when autoscaling many nodes. Commands: 
```
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-xxxx
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=instance-type,Values=p4d.24xlarge
```
If a region is tight, consider capacity reservation or spreading across AZs. Also open a Support > Trusted Advisor check for soft limits.

leo: Azure: quota increases are per subscription and per region. NC/ND series (GPU VMs) need quota change. Use Azure portal to request, or support ticket if you need faster approval. Region SKU availability varies a lot — check https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/global-infrastructure/services/ first. Also watch Public IP and Load Balancer SKUs for high-scale clusters.

cloud-accounts: To open tickets on your behalf we need: project IDs, billing account ID, target regions, desired GPU SKU counts (per region), justification (prod/staging, time window), contact person, and tags/cost center mapping. Put in this template spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.internal/sheets/Acme-Infra-Quota-Req (fill columns A-F).

ana: (typo, ignore)

ana: sorry — ana again. For tags, we follow the pattern: {cost_center, team, env, owner, project_code}. Example tag list: cost_center=acme-sales, team=platform, env=prod, owner=ana, project_code=acme-ml.

samir: Another AWS gotcha: NAT gateway data transfer and per-AZ Elastic IP limits. If you're moving large checkpoints, cost for egress and NAT can balloon. Also we hit per-subnet IP exhaustion when using large node sizes; prefer /20 subnets for GPU pools.

maria: GCP networking gotcha: default VPC is global but subnets are regional; ensure reserved IP ranges are large enough for node pools. If using GKE, reserve secondary IP ranges for pods/services. Example terraform snippet for labels (tags): 
```
resource "google_compute_project_metadata_item" "labels" {
  key   = "labels"
  value = "cost_center=acme-sales,team=platform,env=prod"
}
```
But we usually attach labels at project and resource level.

ryan: IAM baseline we recommend: create dedicated service accounts per workload with least privilege. Roles to consider: roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 (or cloud equivalent), roles/storage.objectAdmin for model storage, roles/iam.serviceAccountUser for infra to impersonate. Also enable org policy to restrict service account key creation.

ana: For cost estimation: ask procurement for estimated on-demand vs committed discounts. Recommend starting with smaller quota requests (can escalate) to avoid being stuck with unused capacity. Also include burst plan: request N GPUs for guaranteed + extra on-demand.

devops-bot: Created support ticket GCP-12345 (GCP quota increase) — link: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/GCP-12345 — assigned to @maria.

devops-bot: Created support ticket AWS-98765 (EC2 quota request) — https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/AWS-98765 — assigned to @samir.

devops-bot: Created support ticket AZ-54321 (Azure quota request) — https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/QuickCreateBlade/overview/id/AZ-54321 — assigned to @leo.

cloud-accounts: I'll open the support requests once the sheet is filled. One more ask: include expected peak tokens/sec or model throughput so we can size node pools and autoscaler profiles.

ana: Will fill the sheet today. Thanks everyone — if there are no other blockers I'll upload project IDs and desired GPU counts by EOD and cc @cloud-accounts. :thumbsup:
